head: 1f82b73a1019930f419492e3e742a96bd43f374e
findings: Generic __atomic_always_lock_free(4,0) is false with -mdisable-hardware-atomics; this is not evidence that all internal-DRAM 32-bit loads/stores block.
IDF __atomic_load_4/store_4 test the pointer against external RAM range first; internal addresses call hardware helper and return without any critical section.
Actual __atomic_s32c1i_load_4/store_4 object code is entry+memw+l32i.n/s32i.n+memw+retw; no call, loop or lock.
EXTRAM fallback has xPortEnterCriticalTimeout with -1, so an idle observer must not put its shared atomic state there.
On this Xtensa port portTICK_TYPE_IS_ATOMIC=1 and TickType_t uint32; xTaskGetTickCount critical macros compile empty.
esp_freertos_hooks.h directly includes portmacro.h, so include FreeRTOS.h and task.h first to avoid the observed recursive-header portYIELD_CORE failure.
recommendedScope: Preserve C atomic semantics and global PSRAM workaround. Explicitly place/align shared state in internal DRAM, validate its internal/aligned addresses before registering hook, and replace the invalid generic compiler static assertion with target-specific checked evidence. No production edit or target build by this reviewer.
